independence: This annotation task inspected only the source PDF and extracted images, not WSPRadar outputs or expected CSVs. The annotator had seen application results during earlier tasks, so this is a retrospective external extraction, not a blinded or preregistered study.
selection_principle: Select the four paper-described temporal density features: early-night negative island, morning positive island, strongest evening positive island, and late-night negative island. For each select the innermost clearly traceable closed contour whose bounding box spans at least the planned 1-hour by 1-dB comparison-cell resolution in both coordinates. This selects enclosing blue/turquoise contours for the two sub-bin night islands and the innermost olive/red contours for the daytime islands. These are feature regions, not confidence intervals or quantiles. Three-hour slices align with the printed major UTC-equivalent ticks and are fixed before comparison.

digitization_uncertainty.basis: Observed antialiased contour strokes occupy about 2-4 pixels; +/-3 pixels covers stroke edge/centre choice and manual bounding-box readout. This is a conservative raster-readout bound, not a statistical confidence interval.

histogram_comparison.meaning: Bounds cover chosen paper contour region plus explicit raster-readout and half-bin localization allowances. They do not include an invented uncertainty allowance for the unknown original smoother.

features.contour: blue enclosed contour around the tiny green negative island
features.interpretation: a negative local density branch; no requirement that a median equal its mode
a positive local density branch; neighbouring lower-SNR branch may coexist

features.contour: innermost red closed contour of the strongest evening density island
features.interpretation: positive high-density concentration; contour level and probability mass are unspecified

features.contour: turquoise closed contour enclosing the sub-bin green island
features.interpretation: negative local branch reappears while a positive branch can coexist; do not require global vertical mode or median to be negative

dawn.basis: The steep contour fan appears approximately between 4 and 6 UTC, consistent with the paper text describing a change near 05 UTC.
dawn.status: contextual check only; the contour fan is not an identified zero crossing of an hourly median or of a unique modal branch

evening.status: approximate prose anchor; the late-night branch annotation provides the concrete visual feature

recommended_matcher.statistic: Local maxima of the vertical density profile in each fixed UTC slice; consider multiple local maxima, including tied plateaus. Do not substitute an hourly median or require the global vertical mode to identify every branch.
recommended_matcher.input: Application paired-observation density counts on the planned 1-hour by 1-dB grid; actual source population/window differences remain separately documented.
recommended_matcher.time_topology: Use periodic boundary conditions in UTC hour; midnight must wrap.
recommended_matcher.smoothing_status: An explicitly declared comparison estimator, not a reconstruction of the undocumented author estimator. Freeze all choices before first evaluation; inspect every grid combination and report absent/unstable features without widening bounds.
recommended_matcher.acceptance_caution: Local-branch existence is limited external corroboration, not proof of the full distribution. Do not derive a numerical density-level or probability-mass assertion from unlabelled contour colours; any extra prominence requirement needs an independently justified frozen rule.

limitations: Original contour levels, kernel, bandwidth, smoothing grid and density normalization are not specified.
Source scatter is visually clipped to -15 through +25 dB. No assertion should treat those limits as the full sample range.
The paper states April 5-7 and UTC but not precise extraction endpoints; population matching is a separate task.
No source-paper exact hourly median, quartile, count or probability mass is inferred.
No WSPRadar output comparison has been performed in this annotation task.
